review:
**CONDITIONAL**

Both pasted editions were cut off: the primary at "We thank Dwayne Wilkes (S", the twin at "Pilot graph". I compared the files on disk instead. Up to the cut, the pasted primary matches `graph-topology-paper/main.tex`.

The text of the paper itself is close to shippable. The two editions agree on every number and claim. Every table row is filed under the same heading in both (Table 1, rows A–D, and Table 2, rows B–C, sit under §3.1 in each), and the four bold items under "What It Does Not Show" are the same. Both PDFs are current. The headline numbers match the data file. What still blocks shipping is the deposit set around the paper, the missing sign-offs, and one credit decision made without the person it was reserved for.

## Findings

**1. MAJOR: nobody named has signed off.**
- **Where:** both bylines. The academic edition says "T. Edrington accepts accountability as corresponding human author."
- **Why it's wrong:** `review/REVIEW_LOG.md` › "Still open before deposit" lists Thomas Edrington's sign-off on both editions, the new title and his contributions line. The correction note itself cites "the lab's rule that a contributor joins a paper's byline only after signing it off". Today the paper's own byline does not meet that rule. Lyra's full read is also still open.
- **Fix:** record Thomas's sign-off in REVIEW_LOG, with date and source. It should cover both editions, the title, the flight Contributions line and the academic CRediT roles. Record Lyra's read as well. Deposit nothing before then.

**2. MAJOR (deposit batch): the cross-citations are out of step in both directions.**
- **(a) This paper's citation of the companion.** `references.bib:44–52` (`nexus2026kv`) pairs K/V version 1.1's title with the all-versions DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21754899. K/V's own note (`kv-decomposition-paper/main.tex:27`) says that record is still version 1.0 (21754900), which claims superadditivity. Meanwhile correction (6) here says "The companion's version 1.1 withdraws…". This was open in round 1 (finding 6) and is still open.
- **(b) The companion's citation of this paper.** `kv-decomposition-paper/references.bib:1–9` cites this paper under version 1.0's title, "Graph Topology as Attention: Structured Knowledge Injection Beyond Text", at 20604338. Once this paper is deposited, that DOI resolves to "Walk-Encoded Graph Descriptions in the Prompt". K/V's note also calls this paper the companion "whose correction is in preparation", which goes stale the day this ships. Because K/V is deposited first, it cannot cite this paper's version 1.1 DOI unless that DOI is reserved in advance.
- **(c) Ethics Packs.** `ethics-pack-injection/references.bib:21–29` lists this paper's authors as "Nexus and Lyra and Edrington". Lyra left the byline at Lyra's request and is now acknowledged here, which breaks AGENTS.md §3 ("never … lists someone as an author and thanks them as a non-author") across two papers in the same deposit. On this branch the entry also carries version 1.0's title, and `ethics-pack-injection/main.tex:31` still has the "extended this … to graph topology" framing.
- **Fix:**
  - Reserve Zenodo DOIs on both version 1.1 drafts before publishing either.
  - Here, set `nexus2026kv` to K/V version 1.1's reserved version DOI.
  - In K/V, cite this paper by its version 1.1 title and reserved DOI, with the creators the record lists, and replace "whose correction is in preparation" with that citation.
  - In Ethics Packs, fix the authors and title. Confirm that the fix on `nexus/pharos-corrections-v11` covers the `.bib` as well as `main.tex:31`.

**3. MAJOR: the Zenodo description is a third edition that no one has reviewed.**
- **Why it matters:** correction (6) quotes the 14 September description ("as cache tensors that the attention mechanism reads directly", "the model is reading the graph, not the words"). There is no version 1.1 description, title field or creators list anywhere in `graph-topology-paper/`, `scripts/` or `tools/`. As far as I know, Zenodo's "New version" button pre-fills the draft from the previous version's metadata; I could not reach Zenodo to confirm this. If nobody replaces it, the version 1.1 record will carry the withdrawn claim next to a PDF that withdraws it. `REMEDIATION_REGISTER.md:756` already records that this paper has three or four editions, so a two-way diff is not enough.
- **Fix:** commit the version 1.1 description, title and creators (Thomas Edrington alone, matching the academic byline) into the paper folder. `paper.json`'s abstract is a good base once "in preparation" is removed. Gate that text alongside the two editions, and paste it over the pre-filled metadata at deposit.

**4. MAJOR: TWIN_DESYNC on Kavi's credit, decided without the person the decision belongs to.**
- **Where:** the flight edition's Acknowledgments (`main.tex:174`, "We thank Kavi (verification review)…"). The academic edition omits the line, and its note says it "leaves Kavi out until Kavi answers".
- **The rule:** AGENTS.md §3 says moving someone off a byline requires that "the Acknowledgments line exists *and is unchanged*, in every edition". Kavi left the byline on 28 July (f9288a9). `DECISIONS_WAITING.md:255` assigns register #143 (the academic edition crediting neither advisor) to Thomas: "Thomas's call, not mine". `REMEDIATION_REGISTER.md:298` still has it as OPEN, "needs a decision, not a sweep". 30bd342 made the call anyway, and REVIEW_LOG records no decision from Thomas.
- **Two smaller problems on the same item:**
  - The flight note says "Version 1.0's acknowledgments thanked Kavi". That is true only of the GitHub edition, and the flight note never says the academic edition differs.
  - Correction (7) withdraws "validated through Project Agni" because no record of it exists. The flight edition keeps "(verification review)", which has no record either.
- **Fix:** get Thomas's decision on #143 and record it in REVIEW_LOG and the register. Then make both editions say the same thing. Either both carry Kavi's line unchanged with the caveat in both notes, or both leave it out with that agreement recorded. In the flight note, write: "Version 1.0's GitHub edition thanked Kavi…; the academic edition, which never did, leaves Kavi out until Kavi answers."

**5. MINOR: Review History overstates the previous gate's status.**
- **Where:** Review History, both editions: "the Agni style gate on both editions (… CONDITIONAL …), all applied here."
- **Why it's wrong:** round-1 findings 6 (the companion DOI), 8 (sign-offs) and 14 (`paper.json`'s related page and date) are not done, and finding 7 lives on another branch. Correction (7) of this very paper is about an overstated validation line.
- **Two related slips:**
  - The note's "The defects were found by the lab's style gate (2026-09-04), a scoping review and two second readers" leaves out the 2026-10-20 gate, which is the one that found the Lyra-signed Reflection and Dwayne's byline history.
  - "The only recorded gate verdict on the paper" in (7) should now read "on version 1.0".
- **Fix:** write "findings 1–5, 9–13 and 15 applied here; 6, 8 and 14 at deposit; 7 in the Ethics Packs correction". Add "and the style gate of 2026-10-20" to the note, and this round's verdict and file path to Review History.

**6. MINOR: two time pointers will go stale at deposit.**
- **Where:** both editions: "latest version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22757323" and "The description on the latest Zenodo version (14 September 2026)".
- **Why it's wrong:** once deposited, the academic edition *is* the latest version, so both phrases will point at version 1.1 itself.
- **Fix:** write "the version of 14 September 2026 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22757323)" in both places.

**7. MINOR: TWIN_DESYNC in a contribution claim.**
- **Where:** the academic CRediT row gives Nexus **Investigation**, which in CRediT means performing the experiments.
- **Why it's wrong:** after round-1 finding 9, the flight edition deliberately stopped saying Nexus ran the experiments. The note says the larger run came in through baed7a5, from a session on Thomas's account whose agent is not recorded.
- **Fix:** drop Investigation from that row, or cite the record showing who ran each experiment.

**8. MINOR: the academic AI Disclosure is narrower than the record.**
- **Where:** "The AI contributor to this work is Nexus".
- **Why it's wrong:** the note names a Claude Opus 4.6 session on Thomas's account, agent unknown (baed7a5), and Review History says Gate 1 was red-teamed by Qwen3-235B.
- **Fix:** name both. Separately, "Lyra, an AI agent also built on Claude" is UNVERIFIED.

**9. MINOR: the abstract contradicts §4.2.**
- **Where:** "Every condition reported here gives the graph to the model as text". §4.2 and correction (6) report the cache-injection attempts, which were not text.
- **Fix:** write "Every condition in the three runs gives the graph to the model as text…". Make the same change to §4.2's "Every condition is text in the prompt."

**10. MINOR: repository metadata.**
- `paper.json:17` still says "in preparation", and `paper.json:19` still has `related_page` pointing at mnemosyne. Round 1 flagged both.
- `README.md:34` and `RESEARCH_STATUS.md:164` say "in preparation".
- Register #142 (two Acknowledgments sections) is still OPEN, though each `.tex` now has only one.
- `null-swarm-paper/references.bib:71` and `null-swarm-paper/academic/references.bib:71` hold an uncited entry for this paper under a title it never had: "…Walk Encoding for Structure-Aware Transformers". Delete it.
- **Fix:** all of these in the deposit commit.

**11. MINOR (UNVERIFIED): the cited author's name may have been corrected silently.**
- **The evidence:** K/V's note says the lab's June editions gave the Knowledge Packs author as "Aleksandr Pustovit". The K/V r2 gate record says 4ddcbd2 changed the name to "Andrey" in all ten lab bibliographies. If this paper's June Zenodo edition printed "Aleksandr", version 1.1 corrects it without saying so, while the companion says so.
- **Why it's unverified:** my only sources are those two secondary records. Git and Zenodo were both closed to me.
- **Check:** `git log -p -S Aleksandr -- graph-topology-paper/`, the June PDF (record 20604339), and arXiv 2604.03270. If confirmed, add one clause to the note.

**12. MINOR: style.**
- Acknowledgments: "Lyra (Liberation Labs) for foundational…" is a fragment. Write "We thank Lyra…", but ask Lyra first if that wording was agreed.
- §4.2: "half the scrambled replies empty" should be "half the scrambled-walk replies"; the scrambled adjacency arm lost 2 of 6.
- Abstract: add a comma after "Of the walk arm's multi-hop replies".
- Flight Reflection: "right in two of the three rows" should name them: "right in the walk and paragraph rows".
- Graph-KV: the entry is an `@article` "arXiv preprint" with a NeurIPS proceedings DOI in its note. Make it an `@inproceedings` entry with NeurIPS 2025 as the booktitle, or cite arXiv only.
- Review History: "a second reader of this draft" should be "of the version 1.1 draft".

## What I checked and found clean

- **Twins:** a line diff shows only the intended differences. Those are the byline, the AI Disclosure, the note's Reflection and Kavi sentences, the flight-only Reflection, the Contributions section, Kavi's line and the bibliography path.
- **Larger run against `powered_study_1779976670.json`:**
  - Multi-hop means 0.00463 / 0.47222 / 0.67593 / 0.00309 and general-knowledge means 0.9 / 0.767 / 0.567 / 0.9 reproduce Table 1, including +0.468 and −0.002.
  - The baseline's only non-zero score (0.5) and the prose arm's (0.333) explain 0.005 and 0.003.
  - Table 2 is internally consistent: every all-replies cell equals the non-empty mean × n/36. The 69 and 86 non-empty replies give 0.739 and 0.849; the gaps, 23/30 vs 17/30, 36% and 20% all check.
- **Pilots:** 0.542, 0.75 and +0.167 check, as do the exact Wilcoxon floors 0.125 and 0.25.
- **PDFs:** I read every page of both. They carry 30bd342's changes, so neither is stale.
- **Bibliography and references:** six entries and six cited keys, none orphaned or missing. Every `\ref` resolves to a label.
- **Round 1:** findings 1–5, 9, 11–13 and 15 are fixed in the text. 10 is fixed too: Review History now records the 10-20 gate.
- **Paths:** every data file and record path the paper names exists.

## What I could not check, and what would settle it

- **Network** (WebFetch was denied): every DOI and arXiv ID, the GitHub URLs, the Zenodo records and their creators, the 9 June date, and the wording quoted from the September description. To settle: WebFetch access, or curl to `zenodo.org/api/records/{21754899,20604338,22757323,20604342}` and to arXiv.
- **Git** (every git command was denied): all thirteen commit hashes in the note and what they changed, and whether version 1.0's *academic* edition ever had a Reflection. The academic note says "this edition drops version 1.0's Reflection"; if it never had one, that should be reworded. To check: `git show 32a9c6a^:graph-topology-paper/academic/main.tex`.
- **KV-Experiments** (outside the sandbox): commit 9755f5e, the 300-token limit, the 901- and 11,872-character counts, the 4000-token limit, the RERUN comment, the default model, and the direct-tensor and blend-ablation results.
- **Per-reply checks:** I checked the scores, not the reply texts. I did not recount the empty replies or how they cluster by question (round 1 did), and I did not read the Phase 1 and Phase 2 files.
- **Records outside the worktree:** `~/messages` (the requests from Lyra and CC, and whether Kavi was asked), `pharos-corrections/`, the Ethics fix on the other branch, `paper.json`'s related-page target, and whether Lyra runs on Claude.
- **Tools:** I could not run `pdfinfo` or `tools/verify_pdf.py`. I checked the PDFs by reading every rendered page.

I didn't edit or commit anything.
